reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes a cold-drawn HEA wire that retains ductile dimple fracture and continuous strain hardening, with no mention of load-induced brittle phase formation or toughness loss. It does not support the key premises that demanding loading causes compositional heterogeneities, brittle secondary phases, or reduced toughness; in fact, it shows the opposite behavior under severe deformation.
premises: High/cyclic loading induces localized compositional heterogeneities in initially single-phase HEAs
These heterogeneities nucleate incipient, brittle secondary phases at stress concentrators
Localized phase transformations lower fracture toughness and promote brittle failure
The baseline single-phase HEA exhibits ductile failure under quasi-static loading
